messages:
viv: Heads-up: intermittent p99 spikes hitting us-east GPU hosts. Different symptom than usual egress policer cases we see long tail only when tenants pull model shards from remote storage + concurrently stream embeddings. Seems like a combo of storage egress + NIC queue pressure causing CPU softirq backlog.

viv: Quick snapshot: some hosts show sustained pci bandwidth busy + userland socket backlog. tcpdump shows many short-lived connections (model shard fetch) + long-lived HTTP streams (embeddings).

viv: ```
# ss -s | grep backlog
Total: 123 (established 45, closed 10, orphaned 0)
TCP: inuse 200 orphan 0 tw 5 alloc 300 mem 5
Socket backlog high on node us-e-12: listen backlog 512, acceptq 400
```

arjun: Interesting. So the noisy behavior is cross-layer: storage pulls spiking PCIe and NIC, then sockets back up and that cascades into higher inference latency. Any tenant correlation?

viv: Yes two heavy tenants (realtime-vision, batch-embeds) overlap. Realtime-vision opens many short fetches for sharded weights; batch-embeds keeps persistent HTT P streams. When they coincide caches thrash and host-level schedulers get saturated.

kel: Two mitigations to try in parallel: 1) eBPF-based per-tenant socket shaping (limit concurrent outbound connections + per-socket rate cap) to reduce PCIe/NIC bursts; 2) ephemeral warm-pool carveout for realtime-vision during their high window so shard fetches hit warm cache, avoiding fetch spikes.

nate: eBPF shaping sounds promising and cheap ops-wise. We have an experimental socket-shaper in canary that can tag sockets by tenant id and enforce limits. Any risk to long-lived streams?

kel: We can exempt long-lived embeddings streams by tag. The idea: limit new short-lived shard fetch connections per-tenant to N per second and add per-conn rate cap. That smooths PCIe bursts.

viv: Rolling it to 10 hosts in the rack now (cmd applied). Rule id sbf-3001. Will route canary telemetry to infra-dashboard.

infra-bot: Action: sbf-3001 applied to tenant=realtime-vision on hosts [us-e-11, us-e-12, us-e-13, us-e-14]. Runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/socket-shaper

arjun: Also pre-authorize ephemeral warm-pool carveout option: if shaping doesn't bring p99 down in 10m, we spin a 1h warm-pool reservation to prefetch shards. Cost estimate for 1h 0.15 slice ephemeral ~ +$Y (billing team will confirm). This avoids kv-cache cold misses.

viv: Canary results after 4m: p95 improved modestly, p99 dropped from ~1.1s -> ~520ms. Socket queue depth reduced in ss output. So shaping helps.

nate: Nice. Keep shaping + monitor. If we still see tail spikes during customer peak test tomorrow, we'll propose ephemeral warm-pool. Add a note about cold-estimate penalty: first 10s of requests may be 100-300ms slower while warm prefetch finishes.

kel: Agree. Also log: if we do weave eBPF at scale, need safety gating (kill-switch) and ensure BPF maps autoscale with host memory. Added a checklist to infra-runbook.

infra-bot: Reminder: paste final timeline and mitigations into INC-9012 and tag billing if carveout used.

viv: Filed INC-9012 with perf graphs + tcpdump snippets. Tagging billing and platform PM for warm-pool option. Monitoring for 30m. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
